subject.title: [Bug]: non_deliverable_terminal_turn produces no outbound notification to channel plugins — Octo (and other channels) go silent

question: Should `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` bypass `message_tool_only` suppression through a narrow core fallback, or should OpenClaw add a plugin-owned terminal-failure hook instead?
rationale: Both viable fixes change user-visible channel delivery semantics, and one option changes the public plugin SDK contract, so automation should not choose the permanent owner boundary.

options.title: Approve narrow core fallback
options.body: Core sends one sanitized failure payload for confirmed non-deliverable terminal turns, after the candidate fix is refreshed and proven with a real SDK-channel run.

options.title: Add a plugin SDK hook
options.body: OpenClaw exposes a documented terminal-failure callback so channel plugins own fallback delivery, accepting public API surface and per-plugin adoption work.

options.title: Keep strict message-tool-only delivery
options.body: Core does not auto-send in `message_tool_only`, leaving visible recovery to plugin-owned workarounds or broader delivery-contract work.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow core fallback
recommendation.body: Core sends one sanitized failure payload for confirmed non-deliverable terminal turns, after the candidate fix is refreshed and proven with a real SDK-channel run.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history is on the auto-reply and follow-up delivery files where the contract decision would be implemented.
